phase: Phase 5 slice 3 - H3-A (geometry) and H3-B (relations), the remaining sub-hypotheses of H3 (Structural Representation)
objective: Does DIRAC-S's pre-fusion visual representation retain single-entity geometric information (H3-A: tumor centroid, extent) and two-entity relational information (H3-B: organ-to-tumor displacement, distance) more so than the parameter-matched CNN/ViT baselines?
note: This is NOT gate_reports/gate_5.json. Gate 5 covers H1-H5 plus the 5 ablations together. Combined with gate_5_h3c_topology.json, this completes H3. This file records H3-A/H3-B's result for the eventual gate_5.json to aggregate.

design.no_injection_confound: Unlike H3-C, neither target is fed to any architecture as an input at any point (nothing in GraphHead or any encoder is handed a per-case geometric/relational ground-truth side-channel the way ph_vector is for DIRAC's topology_head) -- a single fair h-level comparison across all three architectures, no C0/C1 split needed.
design.representation_reused: Same pre-fusion h (mean-pooled) already extracted and cached by jobs/probe_h3_topology_job.py (h3c_{dirac,cnn,vit}_h_c1_{split}.npz) -- no second GPU extraction pass over the same 678 cases.
design.H3-A_target: tumor centroid position (3 dims, z/y/x as a fraction of the mask's own shape) + tumor bounding-box extent (3 dims, fractional per axis). 6 dims total.
design.H3-B_target: organ-to-tumor displacement vector (3 dims, organ_centroid - tumor_centroid, fractional) + its magnitude (1 dim, normalized distance). 4 dims total. Tests the spatial RELATIONSHIP between two distinct anatomical entities (organ label 1, tumor label 2), not either one's own location.
design.fractional_not_absolute: Both targets use fractions of the mask's own shape, not absolute physical units, specifically because the H1 audit confirmed data/preprocess.py's resize_to_fixed applies a per-case zoom factor -- a fractional/relative coordinate is invariant to a uniform per-axis rescale by construction (regression-tested: tests/test_probe_h3ab.py::test_geometry_and_relation_targets_are_fractional_and_scale_invariant), so it sidesteps that confound rather than inheriting it.
design.no_dirac_s_modification: N_DIRAC-S stayed 1,552,520 throughout -- no retraining, no architecture changes, no hyperparameter tuning against this result.

probe: single Linear(dim_in, n_dims) per architecture per hypothesis, MSE loss, Adam lr=1e-2, 300 epochs, re-run at probe-training seeds 0, 1, 2 (same discipline as H3-C, applied proactively here given the seed-0 margins were much smaller/more mixed than H3-C's)
split_policy: probe trained on train split (n=522, 11 cases skipped for missing organ or tumor mask), scored on val split (n=145); test split untouched (spec Section 24)

checks.per_dim_pattern: Centroid_y and displacement components are consistently the weakest/near-zero dims across all three architectures and all three hypotheses -- plausibly because y is not a privileged axis anatomically the way z (roughly cranio-caudal, correlated with organ position within the scan FOV) is; not an architecture-specific effect. The 'distance' scalar (H3-B's 4th dim) is consistently the strongest-recovered dim for all three architectures, notably for CNN (rho 0.48-0.52 across seeds) -- overall inter-entity separation is more recoverable than the directional displacement vector.

status: No DIRAC advantage on either H3-A or H3-B, robust across 3 probe-training seeds -- CNN is consistently at or ahead of DIRAC on both, most clearly on H3-B (relations)
interpretation: A real, seed-robust null-to-negative result for DIRAC on both remaining H3 sub-hypotheses, in clear contrast to H3-C's robust positive gap. H3-A (geometry): DIRAC's small seed-0 edge (+0.006 over CNN) reverses at both other seeds (-0.056, -0.051) -- read as no reliable DIRAC advantage, CNN and DIRAC roughly comparable on average (0.258 vs 0.225) with ViT trailing both. H3-B (relations): CNN is ahead of DIRAC at every single seed (mean 0.214 vs 0.147), the most consistent finding in this slice. Read together with H3-C's result, this is a coherent and informative pattern rather than three disconnected numbers: DIRAC's only clear structural advantage found so far is specifically on topology (H3-C), where jobs/pretrain_dirac_job.py's L_topology gives the encoder an explicit training-time supervisory signal (PHPredictHead(psi,rho) regressed against the real ph_vector) that CNN/ViT's recipe has no equivalent of. Neither geometry nor inter-entity relations have any comparable dedicated loss term in DIRAC's own training recipe -- GraphHead's relational machinery (lattice + learned top-k feature-similarity edges) is trained only incidentally, via whatever gradient L_recon/L_masked/L_struct happen to route through it, exactly the same indirect regime CNN/ViT's own encoders are in for these two properties. The central DIRAC hypothesis -- that the architecture's structural/relational inductive bias produces a general representational advantage -- is NOT supported by this evidence: the advantage found is better explained as 'DIRAC wins where it received explicit topology supervision,' not 'DIRAC's structure generically helps it perceive spatial/relational properties.' This is exactly the kind of finding the project's H0-honesty stance calls for reporting plainly: a real result that sharpens rather than confirms the original hypothesis.
next: H3 is now complete (H3-A, H3-B, H3-C all run). H2 (data efficiency), H4 (uncertainty/magnitude-conflation check), H5 (robustness), and the 5 ablations remain. D_-graph (drop GraphHead) and D_-topology (drop TopologyHead/L_topology) ablations are now specifically well-motivated by this H3-A/B/C pattern -- they would directly test whether removing the un-rewarded graph branch changes anything (predicted: little, given it shows no measurable benefit here) and whether removing the explicitly-rewarded topology branch removes H3-C's advantage (predicted: yes, if the L_topology-training-signal explanation is correct rather than an architecture-alone effect).
